headline: Micron Leads Chip Rebound as Nasdaq Surges 2.69% in Holiday-Shortened Session
body_html:
Chip stocks powered a broad rebound in Friday's shortened post-Thanksgiving session, and Micron was the standout among the market's giants. The memory maker rose 7.60%, shrugging off a brokerage's reduced DRAM price estimates and fresh talk of Huawei developing a rival high-bandwidth memory chip. The Nasdaq gained 2.69% and the S&P 500 added 1.62% before the early 1:00 p.m. ET close.

The rotation was decisive. Semiconductors averaged a 4.67% gain, ahead of Technology at 2.52%, Energy at 2.45% and Materials at 2.08%, while Healthcare, up 0.68%, and Consumer Staples, up 0.69%, trailed. Of the 662 stocks tracked, 563 rose and 97 fell. Sandisk climbed 15.96% and Coherent 14.18%, while Vertex Pharma fell 5.24% and BE Semiconductor Industries slipped 4.06%.

Leadership was uneven among the heavyweights. Broadcom rose 3.83% and TSMC 3.31%, but NVIDIA gained just 0.92% and Apple 0.83%. A rally that favored AI suppliers further down the chain over the best-known names, in thin holiday trading, makes Monday's full session on November 30 a cleaner test of conviction.

briefs.headline: Memory names surge, led by Sandisk
briefs.body: Sandisk jumped 15.96%, the biggest gain in the group, as Micron rose 7.60% alongside it. The memory rally came even as one brokerage trimmed its DRAM price forecasts, suggesting buyers looked past the estimate cut and toward demand tied to AI.

briefs.headline: Optical suppliers catch a bid
briefs.body: Coherent rose 14.18% and Applied Optoelectronics gained 10.48%, putting networking and optical component makers among the day's top performers. The moves fit the wider push into companies that supply the plumbing for AI data centers.

briefs.headline: Tesla climbs on SpaceX merger chatter
briefs.body: Tesla rose 5.22%, with market coverage tying the advance to speculation about a possible combination with SpaceX. Some commentary also questioned whether the stock's valuation already runs far ahead of its earnings, so the rally drew debate as well as buyers.

briefs.headline: Broadcom and TSMC advance; NVIDIA lags
briefs.body: Broadcom added 3.83% and TSMC 3.31%, helped by continued optimism over AI chip revenue. NVIDIA rose only 0.92%, and Apple gained 0.83%, so the biggest names trailed the sector's 4.67% average gain.

briefs.headline: Energy gains as fuel concerns linger
briefs.body: The Energy sector averaged a 2.45% gain. Headlines pointed to a projected diesel market deficit in the second quarter of 2027 and to a Norwegian airline unit's bankruptcy, which was blamed on higher fuel costs tied to the Iran conflict.

briefs.headline: Healthcare and staffing names buck the tide
briefs.body: Vertex Pharma fell 5.24%, Insulet dropped 2.65% and Robert Half slid 3.93%, while Wix.com lost 3.79%. Healthcare's sector average still managed a 0.68% gain, but the laggards stood out in a session where 563 stocks rose and only 97 fell.
